html:
The Castilian War was fought in 1578 between Spain and Brunei. A Spanish fleet from Manila attacked and briefly took the Brunei capital, before disease forced the Spaniards to withdraw.

Spain had taken Manila in 1571 from rulers tied to Brunei, and it wanted to stop the spread of Islam in the islands. Brunei for its part backed Muslim rulers in the south of the Philippines.

Brunei survived, but its power in the north was broken. The Sulu Sultanate grew instead, and the Spanish held Luzon. See also Brunei's golden age.
